惑.meaning: A lonely guard on a sand <part>fort</part> finds a candy <part>heart</part> on the drawbridge each morning, left by a smiling crab. Each day the crab creeps a little nearer, until the guard lets it in for tea. By sunset the crab has the keys, the flag and the cannon. Sweet gifts can <kanji>beguile</kanji> anyone.
惑.on: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' wails the fort's <sound>coo</sound>k when the crab marches out with all her pots and pans.
惑.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, it's a <sound>do</sound>lphin in a crab suit!' cries the guard's little boy, but nobody knows what to believe any more.

久.meaning: A wizard leans his broom in one long <part>slash</part> across a cave <part>entrance</part> and says, 'Back in five minutes.' Moss grows over the bristles, birds nest in the handle, and a whole village springs up around it. He's been gone a <kanji>long time</kanji>.
久.on: Village kids poke the broom with a pool <sound>cue</sound> now and then, just to check it's still real.
久.kun: An old lady in high <sound>hee</sound>ls leaves a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines by the broom every year, in case the wizard comes back hungry.

林.meaning: Two lonely <part>tree</part> saplings are planted side by side on a traffic island. They whisper all night and drop seeds on the passing buses, and soon the roundabout is thick with trunks and squirrels. Drivers now honk their way through a small <kanji>grove</kanji>.
林.on: Deep inside, a squirrel has hidden a stolen gold <sound>rin</sound>g in a hollow trunk.
林.kun: Another squirrel giggles '<sound>Ha</sound>!' and knits a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn into a tiny <sound>shee</sound>t to sleep under between the trunks.

照.meaning: A cave explorer has lost her torch, so she carries a bucket of <part>hot coals</part> and blows on them until they're <part>shining</part> like a tiny sun. Bats wake up, crystals sparkle, and old paintings glow on the walls. Her bucket can <kanji>illuminate</kanji> the whole cave.
照.on: The bats hang upside down and watch, as if it's a light <sound>show</sound> put on just for them.
照.kun: Deep inside she finds a <sound>te</sound>nt someone left there years ago, glowing orange in the light.

武.meaning: A snail ties a toothpick sword to its shell, plants <part>one</part> flag on a <part>stake</part> at the edge of the lettuce bed and paints a <part>stop</part> sign on a leaf. No beetle crosses that line, ever. The garden has found its fiercest <kanji>warrior</kanji>.
武.on: Then the gardener rolls up in a toy <sound>bu</sound>lldozer, and the snail doesn't budge an inch.
武.kun: After the battle, the snail feasts on a crumb of <sound>ta</sound>co and a thimble of tea from a doll's <sound>ke</sound>ttle.

貸.meaning: A hermit crab is late for the beach dance and has no shell, so his friend the <part>shellfish</part> offers a <part>substitute</part>: her spare one, polished and tied with a ribbon. 'Back by Monday, mind.' She's happy to <kanji>lend</kanji> it.
貸.on: To make him look smarter, she adds a tiny bow <sound>tie</sound>, also due back on Monday.
貸.kun: On Monday he returns both with a thank-you gift: a <sound>ca</sound>rp-shaped kite and a box of <sound>su</sound>shi.

称.meaning: A proud farmer waters one stalk of <part>grain</part> with a golden <part>sprinkler</part> until it towers over the barn. The whole village holds a ceremony, and the mayor gives it a grand title: 'Sir Barley the Mighty'. A fine <kanji>appellation</kanji> for a stalk of barley.
称.on: Next year it's the star of the county <sound>show</sound>, wearing a sash with its new name.
称.kun: The cheering crowd showers it with a <sound>ta</sound>co and a jam <sound>ta</sound>rt, and the farmer can't stop beaming.

毒.meaning: A mad scientist hides in an attic with a crooked <part>TV antenna</part> on the roof and a single <part>window</part> painted black. Green fumes curl out of the cracks, and every pigeon that lands on the antenna coughs and flies away. He's brewing <kanji>poison</kanji> up there.
毒.on: At midnight he rows the bottles down to the <sound>dock</sound> and loads them onto a rusty boat.

許.meaning: A troll under the bridge blocks every traveller until <part>noon</part>, when the sun hits his nose and he must make a long <part>speech</part> about his favourite pebbles. When he finally finishes, he yawns and waves you across. Only boredom makes him <kanji>permit</kanji> it.
許.on: Just past the bridge, a little <sound>kio</sound>sk sells the stamped tickets you need to show him.
許.kun: The troll munches a <sound>yu</sound>zu while a <sound>roo</sound>k on his shoulder caws each traveller through.

抗.meaning: The baker's <part>cake stand</part> is bolted to the deck, and when a pirate tries to swing his <part>anchor</part> through the cake, the stand swings right back and bonks him. Plates fly, frosting splatters, and neither gives an inch. That stand will <kanji>confront</kanji> anyone.
抗.on: The pirate retreats to the stern and sulks with an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
抗.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>! <sound>Rah</sound>!' he roars a minute later, charging again with a clove of <sound>ga</sound>rlic as his only weapon.

絵.meaning: During a dull board <part>meeting</part>, a bank clerk pulls a loose <part>thread</part> from her sleeve and twirls it across the table. By the end of the hour it has formed a perfect portrait of the boss, moustache and all. He frames it in the lobby: a woolly <kanji>picture</kanji>.
絵.on: '<sound>Eh</sound>?' grunts the boss, squinting at his own woolly nose, then hangs it up anyway.

幸.meaning: A shipwrecked sailor plants his broken <part>mast</part> in a patch of <part>soil</part> on a tiny island. Next morning it has sprouted leaves, then coconuts, then a branch just right for a hammock. He swings there all day, grinning: pure <kanji>happiness</kanji>.
幸.on: The coconuts turn out to be full of ice cream, so he scoops some into a shell <sound>co</sound>ne.
幸.kun: He sips coconut <sound>ci</sound>der and sighs '<sound>Wah</sound>, what luck!' as the waves roll in.

街.meaning: Right in the middle of the <part>crossroads</part>, someone builds a <part>double mound</part> of earth, like a two-tier cake, and plants palm trees on it. Soon cafés open on every corner and people stroll past in sunhats. The old crossing has become a grand <kanji>boulevard</kanji>.
街.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog leads its owner down the middle, sniffing at every café table.
街.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, look!' shouts a boy, pointing at a shop selling wheels of <sound>chee</sound>se as big as tyres.

推.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> perches on an old <part>anchor</part> half buried in a field, miles from the sea. Where did it come from? A flood? A giant? A flying ship? The bird tilts its head and makes its best <kanji>conjecture</kanji>.
推.on: It decides a pirate dropped it while chasing a <sound>swee</sound>t, and pecks the rust to see if it tastes sugary.
推.kun: Then an <sound>o</sound>ctopus wriggles out of the mud and pushes the whole anchor over.

被.meaning: A farmer nails an old <part>pelt</part> to his <part>weathervane</part> to scare off crows. Instead, the wind spins it so fast that it flings mud, hail and leaves all over his roof. With every storm, the damage his house will <kanji>incur</kanji> doubles.
被.on: Climbing up to fix it, he slips on the mud and snaps the <sound>hee</sound>l off his boot.
被.kun: In the end he pulls the pelt over his head like a hat, while a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond and a <sound>bu</sound>ll in the field stare at him.

爆.meaning: A grumpy chef has an <part>outburst</part> and slams his pan down on the <part>fire</part>, forgetting it's full of popcorn. Kernels shoot up, the lid flies off and the window shatters. The whole kitchen goes off like a <kanji>bomb</kanji>.
爆.on: The blast is so strong it snaps the <sound>buc</sound>kle off his apron belt.
爆.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the waiter, catching a flying kernel in his mouth.

賞.meaning: At the seaside fair, a humble <part>shellfish</part> is held up high on a velvet cushion, glowing in the town's <part>esteem</part>. It won the sandcastle contest by building a whole castle in one night, all by itself. Its shiny ribbon is the top <kanji>prize</kanji>.
賞.on: It bows to the crowd at the end of the <sound>show</sound>, waving one tiny claw.
賞.kun: Everyone praises it with gifts: a <sound>ho</sound>tdog and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon.

香.meaning: A monk dries a bundle of <part>grain</part> stalks in the <part>sun</part> until they're crisp, then lights the tips. Instead of smoke, puffs of fresh-bread smell drift through the temple, and every stomach rumbles during prayers. He has made breakfast-flavoured <kanji>incense</kanji>.
香.on: He stands each stalk upright in an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne so the ash won't fall on the floor.
香.kun: In the temple pond, a <sound>ca</sound>rp sniffs the air, gasps '<sound>Oh</sound>!' and leaps right out over the <sound>ree</sound>ds.

髪.meaning: Your best <part>friend</part> falls asleep at a sleepover, and her <part>long hair</part> keeps growing all night: down the stairs, out the door and twice round the garden. In the morning the cat is tangled in it and the postman is knitting with it. That's a lot of <kanji>hair</kanji>.
髪.on: By noon she has braided enough of it to thatch the roofs of three garden <sound>huts</sound>.
髪.kun: The cat stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, but a <sound>mee</sound>rkat moves in and uses the braids as a hammock.

候.meaning: A weather girl hangs her coat on a <part>coat hook</part>, climbs a <part>pole</part> to a <part>diving board</part> and throws a <part>dart</part> at a map held up with one <part>staple</part>. Wherever it lands, that's tomorrow: snow in the desert, a heatwave on the glaciers. Her darts decide the whole <kanji>climate</kanji>.
候.on: Today the dart hits 'scorching', so she hands everyone in the crowd an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
候.kun: Bowing low like an old servant, she washes the map with <sound>soa</sound>p and walks the long <sound>roa</sound>d home, ready to serve again tomorrow.

刊.meaning: A pirate captain carves his weekly news into planks with a <part>dagger</part>, inks them, and pegs the prints along a <part>drying rack</part> made from the rigging. Gulls carry the copies to every ship at sea. It's the only way to <kanji>publish</kanji> on the waves.
刊.on: Each copy comes with a pressed pink <sound>car</sound>nation tucked inside, to cover the smell of fish.

援.meaning: At the arcade, a <part>claw machine</part> watches a kid fail ten times in a row. On the eleventh try it quietly lowers an <part>anchor</part> from its claw, hooks the biggest teddy and drops it down the chute. The machine has decided to <kanji>abet</kanji> him.
援.on: Then its motor roars like a racing <sound>en</sound>gine, and every prize inside spills out at his feet.

納.meaning: A mouse owes the cat a year of rent, so it pays in <part>thread</part>: spool after spool, wound tight and pushed <part>inside</part> the cat's slipper. The cat purrs and tears up the bill. Debt cleared, everyone happy: a neat <kanji>settlement</kanji>.
納.on: A garden <sound>gno</sound>me signs the receipt as the witness.
納.kun: The cat stores the thread in a drawer, next to a toy <sound>o</sound>ctopus and a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines.

票.meaning: The wind always blows from the <part>west</part>, so the village holds its vote at a hilltop <part>altar</part> and everyone tosses a folded slip into the gale. Wherever the most slips land, that's the winner, and this year it's a goat. Every flying slip is a <kanji>ballot</kanji>.
票.on: The goat's campaign manager, a lady in high <sound>hee</sound>ls, celebrates by spinning a <sound>yo</sound>-yo faster and faster.

誤.meaning: A nervous best man stands up to <part>give</part> his wedding <part>speech</part>, unfolds his notes and reads out his shopping list instead: 'Eggs, socks, a new toilet brush.' The bride laughs so hard she drops the cake. What a <kanji>mistake</kanji>.
誤.on: He hides his red face behind a pair of swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles for the rest of the party.
誤.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' he groans, tangled in a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn from the gift table, while his <sound>ma</sound>ma shakes her head.

斉.meaning: A <part>dancer</part> twirls on top of a football <part>goal</part>, and every time she tips, the coach nudges her back with a <part>pole</part> and draws a <part>slash</part> of chalk where her feet should go. Left a bit, right a bit, until she's perfectly centred. Now she's <kanji>adjusted</kanji>.
斉.on: Satisfied, the coach locks the chalk away in a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe.
斉.kun: Then the whole team lines up neatly on a <sound>so</sound>fa, with a <sound>ro</sound>dent at each end, all exactly alike.

済.meaning: A cat is stuck halfway up a <part>ladder</part> in a storm, and the neighbours argue for an hour about whose job it is. Then the <part>water drops</part> get heavier, the cat jumps into the nearest lap, and everyone goes inside for tea. That's one way to <kanji>settle</kanji> it.
済.on: They toast the end of the fuss with mugs of warm <sound>ci</sound>der.
済.kun: The cat polishes off a plate of <sound>su</sound>shi, and that's the end of that.

句.meaning: A parrot is far too chatty, so its owner tries to <part>wrap</part> its beak in a scarf. But the bird still squeezes one short burst out of its muffled <part>mouth</part>: 'Pass the crackers, please.' Only a few words, yet a complete <kanji>phrase</kanji>.
句.on: On the wall, a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of its clock and repeats it, word for word.

録.meaning: A forgetful gardener writes down every plant she waters, but in <part>gold</part> paint, pouring it from a <part>watering can</part> straight onto the garden wall. Tulips, Tuesday. Roses, twice. Soon the wall glitters with a perfect <kanji>record</kanji>.
録.on: One day she adds a line she can't explain: 'A <sound>roc</sound>ket landed on the lettuce.'
録.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p reads it out loud, and a <sound>roo</sound>k copies it into a tiny notebook.

登.meaning: A mountain goat smells <part>beans</part> cooking inside a climber's <part>tent</part> on the summit, and races up the cliff in the dark, hoof over hoof. By sunrise it's at the top, licking the pot clean. Hunger can make anyone <kanji>ascend</kanji>.
登.on: The climber chases it back down barefoot and stubs a <sound>toe</sound> on every rock.
登.kun: At the top, a <sound>no</sound>mad sits under a tiny <sound>bo</sound>nsai tree, waiting for the next climber.
